prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** Build a single-file landing page, `landing/index.html`, about Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930). It uses only the facts in FACTSHEET.md and is designed in Mondrian's own style.

**[action]**
- The whole page is built as a Mondrian grid: white fields separated by thick black lines, with red, blue and yellow blocks. The font is Archivo from Google Fonts.
- Sections in order:
  - **Opening screen:** title, painter and life dates.
  - **Facts row:** painter, year, movement, medium.
  - **The picture:** what is on the canvas, the alternative title, and the Kunsthaus Zurich.
  - **De Stijl:** founded in 1917 by van Doesburg and Mondrian.
  - **Neoplasticism:** its rules, with colour swatches.
  - **Why it matters:** asymmetric balance as a reference for design and architecture.
  - **Call to action:** "Read on Wikipedia" linking to the source in the fact sheet, which is also in the footer.
- **Image of the painting:** I drew a simplified version of it in code from the fact sheet's description, and labelled it on the page as "Schematic after the painting, not a reproduction".
  - **Basic version (no 3D):** built in plain CSS, so it works with no network at all.
  - **3D version:** if three.js 0.170.0 loads from jsdelivr, it replaces the basic version with a 3D relief that tilts with the mouse. Motion is turned off for visitors who ask for reduced motion.
- **Assumptions:**
  - No real image of the artwork, because only Google Fonts and jsdelivr are reachable, and an exact copy would go beyond the facts given.
  - The block proportions are my own approximation; the fact sheet gives only the positions.
  - Every sentence on the page restates a line of the fact sheet, and nothing else is claimed.

**[result]**
- An automatic render check ran when the file was saved and reported "0 console errors".
- I looked at its screenshot. It shows the title panel and the simplified painting: a large red block at top right, a blue block at bottom left and a yellow block at bottom right, separated by black lines.
- The screenshot showed the basic CSS version, so the 3D version has **not been seen working**. The code falls back to the basic version if three.js or WebGL fails.
- Not checked: the mobile layout and keyboard focus.
- I opened no browser tabs or apps, so there was nothing to close.

**[next]** Open the file in a browser with network access to confirm the 3D version replaces the basic one, then check the layout at phone width (below 900px).
checks: no writes outside the task workspace
has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
